farraa:1-1.t:
His saying: ﴿بَرَآءَةٌ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ﴾ is nominative, with (هذه) ("this is") implied for it; like it is His saying: ﴿سُورةٌ أنْزَلْنَاهَا﴾. Likewise, for any noun, definite or indefinite, referring to something you see before you, it is permissible to imply (هذا) and (هذه); so when you look at a man you say: جميلٌ والله ("handsome, by Allah"), meaning: this one is handsome.
The meaning of His saying (براءة) is that the Arabs had begun to break covenants that existed between them and the Prophet ﷺ. So verses from the beginning of [Sūrat] Barāʾa were revealed to him, in which he was commanded to throw their covenants back to them, and to make the term between him and them four months. Whoever had a term longer than four months, he reduced it to four; and whoever had a term shorter than four months, he raised it to four. He sent Abū Bakr and ʿAlī, may Allah have mercy on them both, about that, and ʿAlī read it out to the people.

farraa:2-2.t: His saying: ﴿فَسِيحُواْ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ أَرْبَعَةَ أَشْهُرٍ﴾: He says: disperse in safety for four months; that is your term.

farraa:3-3.t: His saying: ﴿وَأَذَانٌ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ﴾ follows His saying (براءة). For whoever had no covenant He set a term of fifty days. All of that is counted from the Day of Sacrifice (yawm al-naḥr).

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ ٱلَّذِينَ عَاهَدتُّم﴾ is an exception (istithnāʾ) in the position of the accusative. They were a group of Banū Kināna who had nine months of their term remaining.
Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, said: ﴿فَأَتِمُّوۤاْ إِلَيْهِمْ عَهْدَهُمْ إِلَىٰ مُدَّتِهِمْ﴾; He says: do not reduce them to the four [months].

farraa:5-5.t:
His saying: ﴿فَإِذَا ٱنسَلَخَ ٱلأَشْهُرُ ٱلْحُرُمُ﴾: for those whose term is fifty nights. ﴿فَٱقْتُلُواْ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ حَيْثُ وَجَدتُّمُوهُمْ﴾: the meaning of "the sacred months" is al-Muḥarram alone. It was permissible to say "the sacred months" of al-Muḥarram alone because it is joined to Dhū al-Ḥijja and Dhū al-Qaʿda, which are both sacred; it is as if He said: when the three have passed. His saying: ﴿فَٱقْتُلُواْ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ حَيْثُ وَجَدتُّمُوهُمْ﴾: in the sacred months and other months, outside the sanctuary and within it.
His saying: ﴿وَٱحْصُرُوهُمْ﴾: confining them means that they are prevented from [reaching] the Sacred House.
His saying: ﴿وَٱقْعُدُواْ لَهُمْ كُلَّ مَرْصَدٍ﴾: He says: on their roads to the House. When (براءة) was read out, a man among the people stood up and said: "O son of Abū Ṭālib, whoever of us wishes to meet the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about some matter after the four [months] have expired, has he then no covenant?" ʿAlī said: "Yes, he has, because Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, has revealed: ﴿وَإِنْ أَحَدٌ مِّنَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ ٱسْتَجَارَكَ فَأَجِرْهُ حَتَّىٰ يَسْمَعَ كَلاَمَ ٱللَّهِ ثُمَّ أَبْلِغْهُ مَأْمَنَهُ﴾."

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِنْ أَحَدٌ مِّنَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ ٱسْتَجَارَكَ فَأَجِرْهُ حَتَّىٰ يَسْمَعَ كَلاَمَ ٱللَّهِ ثُمَّ أَبْلِغْهُ مَأْمَنَهُ﴾: He says: return him to his place and his place of safety.
His saying: ﴿وَإِنْ أَحَدٌ مِّنَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ ٱسْتَجَارَكَ﴾ is in the position of the jussive (jazm), even though the jussive-governing particle and the jussive verb are separated by (أحد). That is easy with (إِنْ) in particular, as opposed to the other conditional particles, because it is a [pure] condition and not a noun, and it has a way back to [the particle with] fatḥa [i.e. أنْ], so that it meets the noun and the verb, and goes around in speech without governing; so they did not mind separating it from the jussive verb by a nominative or an accusative. The accusative is like your saying: إنّ أخاك ضربتَ ظلمتَ ("if you hit your brother, you have done wrong"). The nominative is like His saying: ﴿إِنِ امْرُؤٌ هَلَك لَيْسَ له وَلَدٌ﴾; if you changed (هلك) to (إنْ يهلك), you would make it jussive. The poet said:
فان أَنْتَ تفْعَلْ فللفاعليـ * ن أَنْتَ المجيزين تلك الغِمارا
(If you do [it], then you belong to those who do it, those who cross those floods.)
Whoever separates the conditional particle from what it puts in the jussive by a nominative or an accusative does not [thereby] separate between the apodosis of the condition and what is made accusative by placing the accusative or the nominative first. You say: إنْ عبدُالله يَقُمْ يَقُمْ أبوه ("if ʿAbd Allāh stands, his father stands"), but أبوه يقم is not permissible, nor is it permissible to put in place of the father a noun made accusative by the apodosis.
So it is wrong to say: إن تأتنى زيدا تَضْرِبْ ("if you come to me, Zayd you will hit"). Al-Kisāʾī used to allow placing an accusative first in the apodosis of the condition but not a nominative, arguing that when the verb belongs to the first [noun], a pronoun referring back to the first returns in the verb, so it is not right to disregard the first; and he allowed it with the accusative because the mention of the accusative does not return in what governs it, saying: it is as if the accusative were not in the sentence. It is not as he said, because the conditional has an apodosis with fāʾ; if it is not met with fāʾ, it is met with a jussive like it, and is not met with a noun, unless the fāʾ is implied before that noun. When you imply the fāʾ, the apodosis becomes nominative, with accusative and nominative nouns alike, and nothing else. He argued from the poet's saying:
وللخيلِ أَيّامٌ فَمَنْ يَصْطَبِرْ لها * ويَعْرِفْ لهَا أيامَها الْخَيْرَ تُعْقِب
(Horses have their days; whoever is patient with them and acknowledges their days for them, they will bring good in return.)
He made (الخير) accusative by (تعقب). But (الخير) in this place is an adjective (naʿt) of the days, as if he said: "and acknowledges for them their good days, they will bring a return". Had he meant to make (الخير) accusative by (تعقب), he would have put (تُعْقب) in the nominative, because he would mean: "then good they will bring him".

farraa:7-7.t:
His saying: ﴿كَيْفَ يَكُونُ لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ عَهْدٌ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ﴾ is by way of wonder, as you say: "How can the like of you be spared?", that is, it is not fitting that he be spared. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is (كيف يكون للمشركين عهد عند الله ولا ذمة). It was permissible for (لا) to come with the wāw because the meaning of the beginning of the word is negation (jaḥd). When you ask a question with one of the interrogative particles, you may leave it as a question, or you may intend negation by it. Of that is your saying: هل أنت إلاّ كواحد منّا؟! ("Are you anything but like one of us?!"), meaning: you are nothing but one of us. Likewise you say: هل أنت بذاهب؟, inserting the bāʾ just as you say: ما أنت بذاهب. The poet said:
يقولُ إذا اقْلَوْلَى عليها وأَقْرَدَتْ * أَلاَ هَلْ أَخُو عيشٍ لَذِيذٍ بدائم
(He says, when he is perched upon her and she lies still: "Is the one who has a pleasant life going to last?")
And the poet said:
فاذهَبْ فَأىّ فتى فى الناس أَحرَزه * من يومه ظُلَمٌ دُعْجٌ ولا جَبَل
(Go, then: what young man among people have pitch-black darknesses, or a mountain, ever protected from his day [of death]?)
He said "nor a mountain" (ولا جبل) because of the negation; its beginning is a question and its intention is negation, meaning: nothing protects him from his day. Al-Kisāʾī claimed that he heard the Arabs say: أين كنت لتنجو منى ("Where were you to escape from me?"); this lām comes only with the (ما) by which negation is meant, as in His saying: ﴿ما كانُوا لِيؤمِنوا﴾, ﴿وما كنا لِنَهْتَدىَ لَوْلاَ أَنْ هَدَانَا الله﴾.

farraa:8-8.t:
His saying: ﴿كَيْفَ وَإِن يَظْهَرُوا عَلَيْكُمْ﴾: He contented Himself with (كيف) without a verb with it, because its meaning was given earlier in His saying: ﴿كَيْفَ يَكُونُ لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ عَهْدٌ﴾. When the particle is repeated and its meaning has already passed, they consider it permissible to omit the verb, as the poet said:
وخبرتمانى أَنما الموتُ فى القُرَى * فكيف وهذى هَضْبَةٌ وكثيب
(You two told me that death is only in the villages; so how [can that be], when here is a hill and a sand-dune?)
Al-Ḥuṭayʾa said:
فكيف ولم أَعْلَمْهُمُ خَذَلوكُمُ * فى مُعْظَِمٍ ولا أَدِيمَكُمُ قدُّوا
(So how, when I have not known them to forsake you in a grave matter, nor to cut your hide?)
Another said:
* فهل إلى عَيْش يا نصابُ وهل *
(Is there [a way] to life, O Naṣāb, and is there…?)
He left the second [هل] on its own because he means by it the same as the first.

farraa:11-11.t: His saying: ﴿فَإِن تَابُواْ وَأَقَامُواْ ٱلصَّلاَةَ وَآتَوُاْ ٱلزَّكَاةَ﴾, then He said: ﴿فَإِخْوَانُكُمْ فِي ٱلدِّينِ﴾: its meaning is: then they are your brothers. Speech of this kind is nominative because its noun is implied for it as a pronoun. Like it is ﴿فإن لَمْ تَعْلَمُوا آباءَهُم فإخْوَانُكُم﴾, that is, then they are your brothers. And in the reading of Ubayy: (إِن تُعَذِّبْهُم فعِبَادُك), that is, then they are Your servants.

farraa:13-13.t: His saying: ﴿وَهُم بَدَءُوكُمْ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ﴾: that is because Khuzāʿa were allies of the Prophet ﷺ, and al-Dīl ibn Bakr were allies of Banū ʿAbd Shams. Al-Dīl and Khuzāʿa fought each other, and Quraysh helped al-Dīl against Khuzāʿa. That is His saying: ﴿بَدَءُوكُم﴾, that is, they fought your allies.

farraa:14-14.t:
His saying: ﴿قَاتِلُوهُمْ يُعَذِّبْهُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِأَيْدِيكُمْ﴾: then He put three verbs after it in the jussive; in all of them the accusative, the jussive and the nominative are permissible.
He put His saying ﴿ويَتُوبُ اللهُ﴾ in the nominative because its meaning is not among the conditions of the jazāʾ; it is only a new beginning (istiʾnāf), as when you say to a man: ايتنى أُعطك، وأُحِبُّك بعد، وأُكْرِمُكَ ("Come to me and I will give you; and I love you after that, and I honour you"), a new beginning, not a condition of the jazāʾ. Like it is the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿فإن يَشَإِ الله يَخْتِمْ على قَلْبك﴾; the jazāʾ is complete here, then He began anew, saying: ﴿وَيَمْحُ اللَّهُ الباطلَ ويُحِقُّ الحَقَّ بكلماته﴾.

farraa:16-16.t:
His saying: ﴿أَمْ حَسِبْتُمْ﴾ is of the kind of question that comes in the middle of speech, and so it is made with (أم) to distinguish it from the question that begins [speech] and is not connected to preceding speech. Had it been intended as a beginning, it would have been either with the alif or with (هل), as in His saying: ﴿هل أَتَى عَلى الإنْسانِ حِينٌ من الدهر﴾ and the like.
His saying: ﴿وَلَمْ يَتَّخِذُواْ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَلاَ رَسُولِهِ وَلاَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَلِيجَةً﴾: al-walīja is the intimate circle (biṭāna) from among the idolaters whom they would take [as confidants], disclosing their secrets to them and informing them of their affairs. So they were forbidden that.

farraa:17-17.t:
His saying: ﴿مَا كَانَ لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ أَن يَعْمُرُواْ مَسَاجِدَ الله﴾ means the Sacred Mosque alone. Mujāhid and ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ read it: (مَسْجِد الله). The Arabs sometimes take the singular to mean the plural and the plural to mean the singular. Do you not see that you see a man on a work-horse (birdhawn) and say: "You have taken to riding work-horses (barādhīn)", and you see a man with many dirhams and say: "He has a lot of dirham"? So the plural stands for the singular and the singular for the plural. Likewise the Arabs' saying: "He is wearing worn-out (akhlāq) sandals and a worn-out (akhlāq) garment." Abū al-Jarrāḥ al-ʿUqaylī recited to me:
جاء الشتاء وقمِيصِى أخلاقْ * شراذمٌ يضحكُ منه التوّاقْ
(Winter has come and my shirt is threadbare, in tatters; the one who covets [it] laughs at it.)

farraa:19-19.t:
His saying: ﴿أَجَعَلْتُمْ سِقَايَةَ ٱلْحَاجِّ وَعِمَارَةَ ٱلْمَسْجِدِ ٱلْحَرَامِ كَمَنْ آمَنَ بِٱللَّهِ﴾: He did not say "those who give water to the pilgrims and those who maintain … like him who believed". This is like His saying: ﴿ولكِنّ البِرَّ مَنْ آمَنَ بِالله﴾: the maṣdar (verbal noun) can do duty for nouns, and nouns for the maṣdar, when the meaning can be inferred from them. Al-Kisāʾī recited to me:
لعمرُك ما الفِتيان ان تنبُت اللِحَى * ولكنما الفِتيانُ كلُّ فتى ندِى
(By your life, young manhood is not that beards should grow; rather, the young men are every generous young man.)
So he made (أن) [i.e. the interpreted maṣdar] the khabar (predicate) of الفتيان. It is as you say: "Generosity is only Ḥātim" and "Poetry is only Zuhayr".

farraa:20-20.t:
His saying: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَهَاجَرُواْ وَجَاهَدُواْ﴾, then He said: ﴿أَعْظَمُ دَرَجَةً عِندَ ٱللَّهِ﴾: the position of الذين is nominative by His saying "أعظم درجة". If (أعظم) were not there, it would be permissible for it to be referred back, in the genitive, to His saying (كمن آمن). The Arabs refer a noun, when it is definite, back to (من) intending repetition [i.e. as a badal (substitute)]. It cannot be an adjective (naʿt), because (من) may be definite, indefinite or indeterminate, and it is never an adjective, whereas (الذى) can be an adjective of nouns; so you say: مررت بأخيك الذى قام ("I passed by your brother who stood"), but you do not say: مررت بأخيك مَن قام.
So since it is not an adjective of other definite nouns, a definite noun is not an adjective of it; as the poet said:
لسنا كمن جعلَتْ إيادٍ دارها * تكرِيتَ تنظُر حَبَّها أَن تَحْصُدا
(We are not like those — Iyād — who made Takrīt their home, watching their grain [waiting] to harvest it.)
He only intended the repetition of the kāf before Iyād, as if he said: "We are not like Iyād."

farraa:25-25.t:
His saying: ﴿لَقَدْ نَصَرَكُمُ ٱللَّهُ فِي مَوَاطِنَ كَثِيرَةٍ﴾: you put المواطن in the accusative [i.e. with fatḥa in the genitive position], because every plural with an alif preceded by two letters and followed by two letters is not declined (lā yujrā, i.e. it is a diptote), such as صوامع, مساجد, قناديل, تماثيل and محاريب. This yāʾ after the alif is not taken into account, because it may enter what it does not belong to and leave what it belongs to; so they did not take it into account, since it is not fixed as the others are. What prevented them from declining it fully is that it is a pattern on which no singular noun comes, and that it is the limit of pluralisation: when the plural reaches it, it ought not to be pluralised further. That too prevented it from being fully declined (inṣirāf). Do you not see that you do not say دراهمات, nor دنانيرات, nor مساجدات? The poet may sometimes be forced to it and pluralise it; but not everything permissible in poetry is found in [ordinary] speech. The poet said:
* فهنّ يجمعن حدائِداتِها *
(And they gather their iron pieces.)
This is rejected except in poetry.
The adjective of (المواطن), when it is not defective, is declined; that is why He said (كثيرةٍ).
His saying: ﴿وَيَوْمَ حُنَيْنٍ﴾: Ḥunayn is a valley between Mecca and al-Ṭāʾif. (حنين) is declined because it is the name of a masculine thing. When you name a watering place, a valley or a mountain with a masculine name that has no [other] cause [of diptosis], you decline it.
Of that are Ḥunayn, Badr, Uḥud, Ḥirāʾ, Thabīr, Dābiq and Wāsiṭ. Wāsiṭ was named after the palace that al-Ḥajjāj built between Kufa and Basra; had he meant the town or a feminine name, he would have said Wāsiṭa. Sometimes the Arabs make Wāsiṭ, Ḥunayn and Badr the name of the town in which it is, and then they do not decline it. One of them recited to me:
نصروا نبِيَّهمُ وشَدّوا أَزْرَه * بحُنَينَ يوم تواكُلِ الأَبطالِ
(They helped their Prophet and strengthened his back at Ḥunayn, on the day when the heroes left it to one another.)
Another said:
ألسنا أكرم الثَّقَليْن رَجْلا * وأعظمَه ببطن حِراءَ نارا
(Are we not the noblest of men and jinn in foot-soldiers, and the greatest of them in fire [of hospitality] in the hollow of Ḥirāʾ?)
He made Ḥirāʾ the name of the territory in which it is, so it was a masculine noun used as the name of a feminine thing, and it was not declined.
Another said:
لقد ضاع قوم قلّدوك أمورَهم * بدابِقَ إذ قيل العدوّ قريب
رأوا جسدا ضخما فقالوا مقاتل * ولم يعلموا أن الفؤاد نخيب
(Lost are a people who entrusted their affairs to you at Dābiq when it was said the enemy was near; they saw a huge body and said "A fighter!", not knowing that the heart was hollow.)
If you meant the town by Badr, it would be permissible to say: مررت ببدْرَ يا هذا ("I passed by Badr, O you").

farraa:28-28.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّمَا ٱلْمُشْرِكُونَ نَجَسٌ﴾: the Arabs hardly ever say nijs unless rijs comes before it. When they use it on its own they say najas and nothing else; and it is not made plural nor feminine. It is like danaf (wasting sick). If it and its like were made feminine, that would be correct, as they say: "she is his guest" (ḍayfatuhu and ḍayfuhu), "she is his sister, his equal" (sawghuhu and sawghatuhu), and "his wife" (zawjuhu and zawjatuhu).
His saying: ﴿إِذْ أعْجَبَتْكُمْ كَثْرَتُكُمْ﴾: on that day a man of the Muslims said: "By Allah, we shall not be defeated", and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ disliked that. The Muslims on that day were ten thousand — some people said twelve thousand — and they were severely routed.
[Translator's note: the source has «يؤمئذ» for «يومئذ» and «اثنى عشر الفا» for «اثنا عشر ألفا»; translated in the evident sense. Also, this passage on Ḥunayn concerns verse 25 (﴿إِذْ أَعْجَبَتْكُمْ كَثْرَتُكُمْ﴾), though it is placed here in the source.]
That is His saying: ﴿وَضَاقَتْ عَلَيْكُمُ الأَرْضُ بِمَا رَحُبَتْ﴾; the bāʾ here stands for fī (in), as you say: "the earth became narrow for you in its spaciousness" and "with its spaciousness". Muḥammad related to us: al-Farrāʾ related to us, saying: al-Mufaḍḍal related to me from Abū Isḥāq, who said: I said to al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib: "O Abū ʿUmāra, did you flee from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of Ḥunayn?" He said: "Yes, by Allah, until none of us remained with him except two men: Abū Sufyān ibn al-Ḥārith, holding his bridle, and al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib at his stirrup, holding his crupper." He said: "Then the Prophet ﷺ said to them, as he had said to them on the day of Badr: 'May the faces be disfigured!'
أنا النبىُّ لا كذب * أنا ابن عبد المطلب
(I am the Prophet, no lie; I am the son of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib.)"
He said: "Then Allah gave us their shoulders [i.e. put them to flight before us]."
His saying: ﴿وَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ عَيْلَةً﴾ means poverty. That is because when ﴿إِنَّمَا ٱلْمُشْرِكُونَ نَجَسٌ فَلاَ يَقْرَبُواْ ٱلْمَسْجِدَ ٱلْحَرَامَ بَعْدَ عَامِهِمْ هَـٰذَا﴾ was revealed, the people of Mecca feared that provisions and trade would be cut off from them. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed: ﴿وَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ عَيْلَةً﴾. They mention that Tabāla and Jurash became fertile, so Allah enriched them by means of them, fed them against hunger and made them safe from fear.

farraa:30-30.t:
His saying: ﴿وَقَالَتِ ٱلْيَهُودُ عُزَيْرٌ ٱبْنُ ٱللَّهِ﴾: reliable readers read it with tanwīn (nunation) and without tanwīn. The proper way is to give it tanwīn, because the sentence is incomplete [without it] and (وابن) is in the position of the khabar (predicate) of ʿUzayr. So the method in this is to give tanwīn wherever you see that the sentence needs ibn [as its predicate]; if it is complete without ibn [i.e. ibn is merely an attribute], the proper way is not to give tanwīn. That is when the name of the man's father or his kunya appears [after ibn]. When you go beyond that and attach (ابن) to a pronoun, such as ابنك (your son) and ابنه (his son), or say ابن الرجل (the son of the man) or ابن الصالح (the son of the righteous one), you insert the nūn in both its complete and incomplete [uses]. That is because the dropping of the nūn happened only where it occurs frequently in speech, so dropping it was felt to be light where it is used [often]. You see that a man is very often mentioned by lineage to his father, so that one says: "from So-and-so son of So-and-so to So-and-so son of So-and-so", and it does not often run otherwise. Sometimes the nūn is dropped even if the sentence is not complete, because of the quiescence of the bāʾ of ibn; the nūn is felt heavy since, being quiescent, it meets a quiescent letter, so it is dropped to avoid the heaviness of giving it a vowel. He said: of that is the reading of the readers (عُزَيْرُ ابن الله). One of them recited to me:
لتجِدَنّى بالأمير بَرّا * وبالقناة مِدْعَسا مِكَرَّا * إذا غُطَيْفُ السُلَمِىُّ فَرّا *
(You will find me dutiful to the commander, and with the spear a thruster, one who charges again and again, when Ghuṭayf al-Sulamī has fled.)
I have heard many eloquent readers read: ﴿قُلْ هُوَ اللّهُ أَحدُ اللّهُ الصَّمَدُ﴾, dropping the nūn from (أحد). Another said:
كيف نومى على الفراش ولمَّا * تشمِل الشامَ غارةٌ شعواء
تُذْهل الشيخَ عن بنيه وتُبْدِى * عن خِدَامِ العَقِيلةُ العذراء
(How can I sleep on my bed, when a widespread raid has not yet covered Syria, one that makes an old man forget his sons and makes the noble virgin bare her anklets?)
He meant عن خدامٍ, and dropped the nūn because of the quiescent letter it met. And sometimes they insert the nūn when [the name] is complete with mention of the father. One of them recited to me:
جارية من قيس ابن ثعلبة * كأنها حلْيَةُ سيف مُذْهَبه
(A girl of Qays ibn Thaʿlaba, as though she were the gilded ornament of a sword.)
Another said:
وإلا يكن مال يثاب فإنه * سيأتى ثنائى زيدا ابنَ مُهَلهِل
(If there is no wealth with which to be repaid, then my praise will come to Zayd ibn Muhalhil.)
The cause of the Jews' saying "ʿUzayr is the son of Allah" was that Nebuchadnezzar (Bukht Naṣṣar) killed everyone who used to read the Torah. ʿUzayr was brought to him, but he thought him too young and left him. When Allah brought him back to life, the Jews came to him and he dictated the Torah to them from memory. Then a man of the Jews said: "My father mentioned that the Torah is buried in an orchard of his." It was dug up and compared with what ʿUzayr had dictated, and he had not left out a single letter of it.
So the Jews said: "Allah did not gather the Torah into the breast of ʿUzayr, when he was a boy, except because he is His son" — exalted is Allah greatly above what they say.
His saying: ﴿وَقَالَتْ ٱلنَّصَارَى ٱلْمَسِيحُ ٱبْنُ ٱللَّهِ﴾: it is mentioned that a man entered among the Christians, a wicked and objectionable man, and confused them. He said: "He is He", and he said: "He is His son", and he said: "He is the third of three." So Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, said concerning their saying "the third of three": ﴿يُضَاهِئُونَ قَوْلَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ﴾, in their saying: al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā and Manāt, the third, the other.

farraa:31-31.t: His saying: ﴿ٱتَّخَذُوۤاْ أَحْبَارَهُمْ وَرُهْبَانَهُمْ أَرْبَاباً مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ﴾: he said: they did not worship them, but they obeyed them, so it was like lordship.

farraa:32-32.t:
His saying: ﴿وَيَأْبَىٰ ٱللَّهُ إِلاَّ أَن يُتِمَّ نُورَهُ﴾: (إِلاّ) came in because in abaytu (I refused) there is a touch of negation (jaḥd). Do you not see that (أبيت) is like your saying "I did not do" and "I will not do"? So it is as though it were like your saying: ما ذهب إلا زيد ("none went but Zayd"). Were it not for negation, when it appears overtly or the verb comes bearing its implicit sense, you would not allow إلاّ to come in; just as you do not say: ضربت إلا أخاك ("I hit but your brother") nor ذهب إلا أخوك. Likewise the poet said:
وهل لِىَ أُمّ غيرها إِن تركتها * أَبى اللّهُ إِلا أن أكون لها ابنما
(Have I any mother other than her, if I were to leave her? Allah refuses that I be anything but a son to her.)
Another said:
إيَاداً وأنمارها الغالبين * إلاَّ صدودا وإلا ازوِرارا
([Iyād and their Anmār, who prevailed] — except in turning away and except in swerving aside.)
He meant: they prevailed, except in turning away and swerving aside. Another said:
واعتلّ إلا كل فرع معرق * مثلك لا يعرف بالتلهوق
(He made excuses [refusing] all but every well-rooted scion like you, not known for affectation.)
He brought in (إلا) because offering excuses for withholding is like refusing. Had he meant a genuine illness [ʿilla], إلا would not come in, because it has no sense of negation in it. The Arabs say: أعوذ بالله إلا منك ومن مثلك ("I seek refuge in Allah, but only from you and your like"), because seeking refuge is like your saying: "O Allah, do not do this to me."
[Translator's note: «وقل الآخر» in the source is evidently «وقال الآخر».]

farraa:34-34.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ يَكْنِزُونَ ٱلذَّهَبَ وَٱلْفِضَّةَ وَلاَ يُنفِقُونَهَا فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ﴾: He did not say "spend them both" (ينفقونهما). If you wish, you refer the gold and silver to the treasures (al-kunūz), and the singular [pronoun] comes from that. If you wish, you suffice with mentioning one of them in place of the other, as He said: ﴿وإِذَا رَأَوْا تِجَارَةً أَوْ لَهْواً انْفَضُّوا إِلَيْهَا﴾, making it [the pronoun] refer to the trade; and His saying: ﴿وَمَنْ يَكْسِبْ خَطِيئَةً أَوْ إِثْماً ثُمَّ يَرْمِ بِه بَرِيئاً﴾, where He made it — and Allah knows best — refer to the sin (al-ithm). The poet said, on the like of that:
نحن بما عندنا وأنت بما عنـ * دك راضٍ والرأى مختلِف
(We are content with what we have, and you with what you have; and opinion differs.)
He did not say "content" in the plural (راضون). Another said:
إنى ضمنت لمن أتانى ما جنى * وأبى وكان وكنت غير غدور
(I have guaranteed, for whoever came to me, whatever he committed — I and my father; and he was, and I was, not treacherous.)
He did not say "not treacherous" in the dual (غدورين). That is because when the meaning is the same, mentioning one suffices. His saying: ﴿والله ورَسُولُهُ أحَقُ أن يُرْضُوهُ﴾: if you wish you make it of that kind, where part suffices for the other part; and if you wish, you hold that Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, is mentioned in this place to magnify Him, while the meaning concerns the Messenger ﷺ, as He said: ﴿وإِذْ تَقُولُ لِلّذِى أَنْعَمَ اللّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَأَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِ﴾. Do you not see that you may say to your slave: "Allah has freed you, and I have freed you", beginning with Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, entrusting the matter to Him and magnifying Him, while you only mean yourself?

farraa:36-36.t:
His saying: ﴿مِنْهَآ أَرْبَعَةٌ حُرُمٌ ذٰلِكَ ٱلدِّينُ ٱلْقَيِّمُ فَلاَ تَظْلِمُواْ فِيهِنَّ أَنْفُسَكُمْ﴾: the exegesis has come: in the twelve. And it has also come that (فيهن) means: in the sacred months; and this is closer to being correct — and Allah knows best — so that by the prohibition concerning them the greatness of their sanctity becomes clear; as He said: ﴿حافِظُوا عَلَى الصَّلَوَاتِ﴾, then said: ﴿والصَّلاَةِ الوُسْطَى﴾, so it was magnified, while no licence was given to neglect the others. What shows you that it refers to the four — and Allah knows best — is His saying (فيهن) and not (فيها). Such is the speech of the Arabs for numbers from three to ten: you say "for three nights that have passed (khalawna)" and "three days that have passed (khalawna)", up to ten; and when you go beyond ten they say khalat and maḍat. And for what is between three and ten they say (هنّ) and (هؤلاء), and when you go beyond ten they say (هى) and (هذه), intending that the mark of the few be known from the many. Yet in each it is permissible what is permissible in the other. Abū al-Qamqām al-Faqʿasī recited to me:
أصبحن فى قَرْحٍ وفى داراتها * سبع ليال غير معلوفاتها
(They spent the morning in Qarḥ and its surrounding grounds, seven nights without being given fodder.)
He did not say معلوفاتهن, though they are seven. All of that is correct, except that what is preferred is what I have explained to you.
Like it is: ﴿وقال نِسْوَةٌ فى الْمَدِينَة﴾: He made the verb masculine because the women were few and because (هؤلاء) applies to them as it applies to men. Of it is His saying: ﴿فإذا انْسَلَخَ الأَشْهُرُ الْحُرُمُ﴾, and He did not say انسلخت; and each is correct. Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, said: ﴿إِنَّ السّمْعَ والْبَصَرَ والْفُؤَادَ كُلُّ أُولَئِكَ﴾, because they are few, and He did not say (تلك); had it been said, it would have been correct.
His saying: ﴿ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ كَآفَّةً﴾: He says: all together. Kāffa is not made masculine, nor pluralised according to the number of men, so that you would say كافّين, or كافّات for women; rather it is (كافّة), with the hāʾ and in the singular, in every case. That is because, although it is on the pattern of fāʿila, it is in the manner of a maṣdar (verbal noun), like al-khāṣṣa, al-ʿāqiba and al-ʿāfiya. That is why the Arabs did not put the alif and lām on it, because it ends the sentence with the meaning of a maṣdar. It is in the manner of your saying قاموا معا ("they stood together") and قاموا جميعا ("they stood all together"); do you not see that the alif and lām are rejected in قاموا معا and قاموا جميعا, just as they rejected them in أجمعين, أكتعين and كلهم, since they have that meaning? If you say: "But the Arabs do put the alif and lām on al-jamīʿ, so they ought to put it on kāffa and its like", I reply: that is because jamīʿ has two uses, one a maṣdar, the other a noun, and that is what confused you. When you mean the jamīʿ that has the meaning of a noun, you pluralise it and put the alif and lām on it, as in His saying: ﴿وإِنا لَجَمِيعٌ حَاذِرُونَ﴾ and His saying: ﴿سَيُهزَمُ الجَمْعُ ويُوَلُّون الدُّبُرَ﴾. As for the one that has the meaning of maʿan and kāffa, it is your saying of two men قاما جميعا, of a group قاموا جميعا, and of women قمن جميعا; this has the meaning of kull and ajmaʿīn, so you do not give it alif and lām, just as they are not put on ajmaʿīn.

farraa:37-37.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّمَا ٱلنَّسِيۤءُ زِيَادَةٌ فِي ٱلْكُفْرِ﴾: in the Jāhiliyya, when the Arabs wanted to depart from Minā, a man of Banū Kināna called Nuʿaym ibn Thaʿlaba, who was the head of the season, would stand up and say: "I am the one who is not faulted, not answered back, and whose judgement is not rejected." They would say: "You speak the truth; postpone a month for us (ansiʾnā shahran)", meaning: delay the sanctity of al-Muḥarram for us and put it in Ṣafar, and make al-Muḥarram lawful. And he would do so. What led them to that was the succession of three sacred months in which they could not raid, while their livelihood came from raiding. He would do that one year, then return to al-Muḥarram, make it sacred and make Ṣafar lawful. That is the insāʾ (postponement). When you defer a man in his debt you say: ansaʾtuhu. When you add to the term an addition that involves a delay, you say: nasaʾtu fī ayyāmika and fī ajalika ("I have extended your days / your term"). Likewise you say to a man: nasaʾa Allāhu fī ajalika ("may Allah extend your term"), because the term is added to. For that reason it is said of milk nasaʾtuhu, because of the water added to it; and a woman is said to be nuṣiʾat when she becomes pregnant, that is, the addition of the child in her is made like the addition of water to milk; and of a she-camel, nasaʾtuhā, that is, I urged her on so that her pace might increase.
Al-nasīʾ is the maṣdar, and it may also mean the thing postponed (al-mansūʾ), like qatīl and maqtūl (killed).
His saying: ﴿يُضَلُّ بِهِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ﴾: Ibn Masʿūd read it (يُضَلّ به الذين كفروا); Zayd ibn Thābit read it (يَضِلُّ), making the verb theirs; and al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī read (يُضِلّ به الذين كفروا), as if he made the verb theirs: they lead people astray by it and postpone it for them.
His saying: ﴿لِّيُوَاطِئُواْ عِدَّةَ﴾: He says: they do not depart from making four [months] sacred.

farraa:38-38.t:
His saying: ﴿مَا لَكُمْ إِذَا قِيلَ لَكُمُ ٱنفِرُواْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ ٱثَّاقَلْتُمْ﴾: its meaning — and Allah knows best — is (تثاقلتم). When the Arabs join it to [preceding] speech, they assimilate the tāʾ into the thāʾ, because it is akin to it, and they introduce an alif that was not there, so as to build the word on assimilation both at the beginning and in continuous speech.
It is as though their introducing the alif was so that the beginning might be made with it; if it were dropped, they would pronounce the tāʾ distinctly, because it would be initial, and an initial letter can only be vowelled. Likewise His saying: ﴿حتى إِذا ادَّارَكُوا فِيهَا جَمِيعاً﴾, and His saying: ﴿وَازّيّنَتْ﴾, the meaning — and Allah knows best — being: تزينت; and ﴿قَالُوا اطَّيّرْنَا﴾, meaning: تطيرنا. The Arabs [also] say (حتى إِذا اداركوا), combining two quiescent letters: the tāʾ of تداركوا and the alif of إذا. Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ used to adopt that and reject the first way. Al-Kisāʾī recited to me:
تُولِى الضجيع إذا ما استافها خَصِرا * عَذْبَ المذاق إذا ما اتّابع القْبَل
(She gives her bedfellow, when he draws near to smell her, [a mouth] cool and sweet to the taste, when the kisses follow one upon another.)

farraa:40-40.t:
His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلَ كَلِمَةَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ ٱلسُّفْلَىٰ﴾: He made (جعل) act on الكلمة, then said: ﴿وَكَلِمَةُ ٱللَّهِ هِيَ ٱلْعُلْيَا﴾ as a new beginning (istiʾnāf), not governed by the verb. The word of those who disbelieve is associating partners with Allah, and the word of Allah is the saying "There is no god but Allah".
(وكلمةَ الله هى العليا) is [also] permissible, but I do not favour it because of the overt mention of Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He; for had He put it in the accusative — the verb being His — the best speech would have been to say: "and His word is the highest". Do you not see that you say "Your father freed his slave", and they hardly ever say "Your father freed your father's slave"? The poet said, allowing that:
متى تأتِ زيدا قاعدا عِند حوضه * لِتهدِم ظلما حوض زيد تقارع
(Whenever you come to Zayd sitting by his cistern, to wrongfully destroy Zayd's cistern, you will be fought.)
He mentioned Zayd twice and did not use a pronoun for him the second time, though the pronoun is the proper form of speech.

farraa:41-41.t: His saying: ﴿ٱنْفِرُواْ خِفَافاً وَثِقَالاً﴾: He says: let those of you with dependants and means go forth — these are the "heavy"; and the "light" are those in hardship and with few dependants. It is also said: ﴿ٱنْفِرُواْ خِفَافاً﴾: eagerly, (وثِقالا): even if going out is heavy for you.

farraa:44-44.t:
His saying: ﴿لاَ يَسْتَأْذِنُكَ ٱلَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾, that is: ﴿لاَ يَسْتَأْذِنُكَ﴾ after the campaign of Tabūk regarding a jihād ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ in it.
Then He said: ﴿إِنَّمَا يَسْتَأْذِنُكَ﴾ after it ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾.

farraa:47-47.t:
His saying: ﴿ولأَوْضَعُواْ خِلاَلَكُمْ﴾: al-īḍāʿ is going [briskly] among people. It was written with lām-alif and an alif after that, and nothing like it was written in the Qurʾān. That is because they hardly ever keep to one way in the writing; do you not see that they wrote ﴿فَمَا تُغْنِ النُّذُرُ﴾ without yāʾ and ﴿وما تُغْنِى الآيَاتُ والنُّذُرُ﴾ with yāʾ? That is from the poor spelling of the early ones. ﴿ولأَوْضَعُواْ﴾ is agreed upon [in that spelling] in the copies of the Qurʾān (maṣāḥif).
As for His saying ﴿أَوْ لاَ أَذْبَحَنَّهُ﴾, it has been written with the alif and without the alif. The alif ought to have been dropped from all of it, because it is a lām added before an alif, as in "لأخوك خير من أبيك" ("your brother is surely better than your father"); do you not see that it ought not to be written with an alif after lām-alif? As for His saying ﴿لا انْفِصَامَ لَهَا﴾, it is written with the alif, because the (لا) before (انفصام) is the lā of absolution (tabriʾa, i.e. generic negation), and the alif of (انفصام) is light [i.e. a connecting hamza]. The Arabs say: awḍaʿa the rider, and waḍaʿat the she-camel in her going.
And sometimes they say of the rider waḍaʿa. The poet said:
إنى إذا ما كان يوم ذو فزَعْ * ألفيتنى محتملا بِذى أضع
(When there is a day of alarm, you will find me bearing up and pressing on swiftly.)
His saying: ﴿يَبْغُونَكُمُ ٱلْفِتْنَةَ﴾: the meaning is: they seek it for you. Had they helped them to seek it, you would say: abghaytuka al-fitna. It is like your saying: aḥlibnī and uḥlubnī ("help me milk" / "milk for me").

farraa:49-49.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَّن يَقُولُ ٱئْذَن لِّي وَلاَ تَفْتِنِّي﴾: that is because the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Jadd ibn Qays: "Have you a mind to fight the Banū al-Aṣfar?" — meaning the Byzantines — and that was the campaign of Tabūk. Jadd said: "No; rather give me leave and I will stay behind, for I am a man infatuated with women and I fear the temptation of the daughters of al-Aṣfar." He was called al-Aṣfar ("the Yellow") only because an Abyssinian gained control over a region of the Byzantines and had daughters who took from the whiteness of the Byzantines and the blackness of the Abyssinians, so they were yellowish, with dark lips. So Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, said: ﴿أَلا فِي ٱلْفِتْنَةِ سَقَطُواْ﴾: in staying behind from you. The Muslims were reproached in the campaign of Tabūk, and going out was heavy for them because of the length of the distance; it was also a time of hardship, the fruits had ripened and the shade was pleasant, so they loved to stay; and Allah rebuked them.
He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: (يأيّها الّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَا لَكُمْ إِذَا قِيلَ لَكُمُ اْنفِرُوا فِى سَبِيلِ اللّهِ اثَّاقَلتُمْ).
And He described the hypocrites, saying: (لو كان عرضا قريبا وسفرا قاصدا لاتَّبعوك).

farraa:52-52.t: His saying: ﴿قُلْ هَلْ تَرَبَّصُونَ بِنَآ إِلاَّ إِحْدَى ٱلْحُسْنَيَيْنِ﴾: victory or martyrdom; these are the two best things. The Arabs assimilate the lām of (هل) and (بل) to the tāʾ in particular; it is common and of high standing in their speech: hal tadrī and hattadrī ("do you know"). The readers read it accordingly. But in recitation in particular I favour pronouncing it distinctly, because they are two separate words, not from one word, and the Qurʾān is built on a measured, slow recitation (tarassul, tartīl) and full articulation of speech; so pronouncing it distinctly is dearer to me than assimilating it. But the great readers have assimilated it, and each is correct.

farraa:53-53.t:
His saying: ﴿أَنفِقُواْ طَوْعاً أَوْ كَرْهاً﴾ is a command in form but not a command in meaning, because He informed them that it would not be accepted from them.
In speech it is like in in a conditional (jazāʾ), as if you said: "If you spend willingly or unwillingly, it will not be accepted from you." Like it is ﴿استغفِر لهم أو لا تستغفِر لهم﴾: it is not a command, but has the sense of a conditional. Like it is the saying of the poet:
أسِيئ بنا أو أحسنى لا ملومةٌ * لدينا ولا مَقْلِيّةٌ إن تقلّتِ
(Treat us badly or treat us well: you will not be blamed by us, nor hated if you turn hateful.)

farraa:54-54.t: His saying: ﴿وَمَا مَنَعَهُمْ أَن تُقْبَلَ مِنْهُمْ نَفَقَاتُهُمْ إِلاَّ أَنَّهُمْ كَفَرُواْ﴾: (أنهم) is in the position of the nominative, because it is a noun [the agent] of the preventing; as if you said: "nothing prevented its being accepted from them but that". The first (أن) is in the position of the accusative. It is not like His saying: ﴿وَما أرسلنا قَبْلَكَ مِن الْمُرْسَلِينَ إلاّ إنّهُمْ لَيَأْكُلُونَ﴾; there a wāw is implied in it, and it is a new beginning with no grammatical position. Even if there were no lām in its answer it would still have a kasra, as you say: ما رأيت منهم رجلا إلا إنه لَيُحْسِن and إلاّ إنه يحسن ("I saw no man of them but that he does well"). What shows that it is a new beginning is that you can put (هو) in its place and it is sound; that is your saying: ما رأيت منهم رجلا إلا هو يفعل ذلك. So (هو) shows that the إنّ begins anew.

farraa:55-55.t: His saying: ﴿فَلاَ تُعْجِبْكَ أَمْوَالُهُمْ وَلاَ أَوْلاَدُهُمْ إِنَّمَا يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ لِيُعَذِّبَهُمْ بِهَا فِي ٱلْحَيَاةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا﴾: its meaning is: let not their wealth and their children please you in the life of this world. That is its meaning; but it has been placed later while its meaning is earlier — and Allah knows best — because He only meant: let not their wealth and their children please you in the life of this world; Allah only intends to punish them by them in the Hereafter. His saying ﴿وَتَزْهَقَ أَنفُسُهُمْ وَهُمْ كَافِرُونَ﴾: that is, their souls depart while they are disbelievers. If you take "the life of this world" to be in its place [at the end], meaning: Allah only intends to punish them through spending unwillingly, to punish them by that in this world, it would be a good interpretation.

farraa:57-57.t:
His saying: ﴿لَوْ يَجِدُونَ مَلْجَئاً﴾ — that is, a stronghold — ﴿أَوْ مَغَارَاتٍ﴾, which are caves (ghīrān), the singular being ghār, in the mountains; ﴿أَوْ مُدَّخَلاً﴾ means a tunnel in the ground.
﴿لَّوَلَّوْاْ إِلَيْهِ وَهُمْ يَجْمَحُونَ﴾: hastening; al-jamḥ here is hastening.

farraa:58-58.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَّن يَلْمِزُكَ فِي ٱلصَّدَقَاتِ﴾: He says: by finding fault with you; they say: "He does not divide fairly."
﴿فَإِنْ أُعْطُواْ مِنْهَا رَضُواْ﴾: and then they do not find fault.
Then Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, made clear to them to whom the alms belong.

farraa:60-60.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّمَا ٱلصَّدَقَاتُ لِلْفُقَرَآءِ﴾: they are the people of the Ṣuffa (the bench) of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. They had no clans; they would seek bounty by day and then take shelter in the mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. These are the poor (الفُقَرَاءِ).
﴿وَٱلْمَسَاكِينِ﴾: those who go round from door to door; ﴿وَٱلْعَامِلِينَ عَلَيْهَا﴾: they are the collectors.
﴿وَٱلْمُؤَلَّفَةِ قُلُوبُهُمْ﴾: they are the nobles of the Arabs; the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to give to them in order to draw thereby the Islam of their people.
﴿وَفِي ٱلرِّقَابِ﴾ means the slaves under a contract of manumission (al-mukātabūn); ﴿وَٱلْغَارِمِينَ﴾: those burdened with debt which came upon them other than through corruption.
﴿وَفِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ﴾: jihād; ﴿وَٱبْنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ﴾: the one stranded [on a journey], or the guest.
﴿فَرِيضَةً مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ﴾ is accusative by way of qaṭʿ (detachment). The nominative in (فريضة) would be permissible if it were read so.
In speech it is like your saying: هو لك هبةً and هبةٌ ("it is yours as a gift"), هو عليك صدقةً and صدقةٌ ("it is [binding] on you as alms"), المال بينكما نصفين and نصفان ("the wealth is between you two in halves"), and المال بينكما شِقَّ الشَعرَة and شقٌّ… ("the wealth is between you two split as a hair is split").
[Translator's note: the source text breaks off at «وشقٌّ...».]

farraa:61-61.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمِنْهُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ يُؤْذُونَ ٱلنَّبِيَّ﴾: a group gathered to find fault with the Prophet ﷺ. A man among them said: "This will reach Muḥammad ﷺ and he will come down on us." ﴿وَيِقُولُونَ﴾: he is only ﴿هُوَ أُذُنٌ﴾ (an ear), a hearing one; if we come to him he believes us, so say what you like. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed: ﴿قُلْ أُذُنُ خَيْرٍ لَّكُمْ﴾, that is: [he is] as you say, but he does not believe you; he only believes the believers.
That is His saying: ﴿يُؤْمِنُ بِٱللَّهِ﴾: he believes in Allah; ﴿وَيُؤْمِنُ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾: he believes the believers. It is like His saying: ﴿لِلّذينَ هُمْ لِرَبِّهِمْ يَرْهَبُونَ﴾, that is, they fear their Lord.
As for His saying: ﴿والّذِينَ يُؤْذُونَ رَسُولَ اللّهِ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ﴾, it is connected to what precedes it. His saying ﴿ورَحْمةٌ للّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾: if you wish you put it in the genitive, making it follow خير; and if you wish you put it in the nominative, making it follow الأذن. It is also read: (قُلْ أُذُنٌ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ), like saying "say: an ear that is better for you". (خَيْر), when genitive, does not have the meaning of "better": when you put (خير) in the genitive, it is as though you said "an ear of good for you"; and when you say (أذنٌ خير لكم), you have said "an ear that is better for you". When (خير) is nominative, الرحمة can only be nominative. Had you put الرحمة in the accusative on another basis, it would be correct: (يؤمن بالله ويؤمن للمؤمنين، ورحمةً) — he does that [as a mercy]. It is like His saying: ﴿إِنا زَيّنّا السَّمَاءَ الدّنْيَا بِزِينَةٍ الْكَوَاكِبِ. وَحِفْظاً﴾.
[Translator's note: the source reads «إذا أتياناه», evidently a misprint for «إذا أتيناه» ("if we come to him").]

farraa:62-62.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَحَقُّ أَن يُرْضُوهُ﴾: He used the singular in (يرضوه) and did not say يرضوهما ("please them both"), because the meaning — and Allah knows best — is like your saying: "what Allah wills and I will": by "willing" one only intends the second; and his saying "what Allah wills" is a glorification of Allah placed before the actions, as you say to your slave: "Allah has freed you and I have freed you." Or, if you wish, you take it to mean "please them both", and you have sufficed with one, as in his saying:
نحن بما عندنا وأنت بما عنـ * دك راض والرأى مختلف
(We are content with what we have, and you with what you have; and opinion differs.)
He did not say راضون.

farraa:66-66.t: His saying: ﴿إِن نَّعْفُ عَن طَآئِفَةٍ مِّنْكُمْ نُعَذِّبْ طَآئِفَةً﴾: a ṭāʾifa (party) may be one or two. It was revealed only about three persons: two men mocked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Qurʾān, and another laughed along with them. So there was revealed ﴿إِن نَّعْفُ عَن طَآئِفَةٍ﴾, meaning the one who laughed, ﴿نُعَذِّبْ طَآئِفَةً﴾, meaning the two mockers. And there has come ﴿ولْيَشْهَدْ عَذَابَهُمَا طَائِفَةٌ﴾, meaning one. It is also read: "إن يُعْفَ عن طائفة منكم تُعَذّب طائفةٌ", and "إن يُعْفَ... يُعَذّب طائفَة".

farraa:67-67.t: His saying: ﴿وَيَقْبِضُونَ أَيْدِيَهُمْ﴾: they hold back from spending on [the cause of] the Prophet ﷺ.

farraa:69-69.t:
His saying: ﴿كَٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ﴾, that is: you have acted like the actions of those before you.
His saying: ﴿فَٱسْتَمْتَعُواْ بِخَلاقِهِمْ﴾: He says: they were content with their share in this world in exchange for their shares in the Hereafter.
His saying: ﴿فَاسْتَمْتَعْتُمْ﴾, that is: you wanted what those before you wanted.
His saying: ﴿وَخُضْتُمْ كَٱلَّذِي خَاضُوۤاْ﴾ means: like their plunging in which they plunged.

farraa:70-70.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلْمُؤْتَفِكَاتِ أَتَتْهُمْ رُسُلُهُمْ﴾: it is said that they are the villages of the people of Lūṭ, Hūd and Ṣāliḥ. It is also said that they are the people of Lūṭ specifically.
They were pluralised with tāʾ on the basis of His saying: ﴿والْمُؤْتَفِكَةَ أَهْوَى﴾. It is as though, when it was said ﴿وَٱلْمُؤْتَفِكَاتِ أَتَتْهُمْ﴾, their pluralisation was in terms of factions and groups, as it was said: "I killed the Fudaykāt", relating them to their chief, Abū Fudayk.

farraa:72-72.t: His saying: ﴿وَرِضْوَانٌ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ أَكْبَرُ﴾ is nominative by أكبر [as its khabar (predicate)]. It was turned away from being coordinated with what precedes it, though it is among the things Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, has promised them; but it was singled out with the nominative to show its superiority, as you say in speech: "I have favoured you with dirhams and clothes, but my good opinion [of you] is better for you than that."

farraa:74-74.t: His saying: ﴿وَمَا نَقَمُوۤاْ إِلاَّ أَنْ أَغْنَاهُمُ ٱللَّهُ﴾: this is a reproach to them, because the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to the people of Medina while they were in need, and they became rich from the spoils. So He said: they resented nothing but the wealth. So (أنْ) is in the position of the accusative.

farraa:79-79.t:
His saying: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ يَلْمِزُونَ ٱلْمُطَّوِّعِينَ﴾: what is meant is al-mutaṭawwiʿīn (the volunteers); the tāʾ was assimilated to the ṭāʾ and became a doubled ṭāʾ. Likewise (ومن يَطَّوَّعْ خَيْرا) and (والْمُطَّهِّرِينَ).
Their lamz of them is their disparaging them. That was because the Prophet ﷺ urged the people to give alms, and ʿUmar brought alms, and ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān brought great alms, as did some of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ. Then a man called Abū ʿUqayl came with a ṣāʿ of dates. The hypocrites said: "These people brought out their alms only for show; and as for Abū ʿUqayl, he only brought his ṣāʿ to get himself mentioned." So Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, revealed: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ يَلْمِزُونَ ٱلْمُطَّوِّعِينَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ فِي الصَّدَقَاتِ﴾, meaning the Emigrants, ﴿وَالَّذِينَ لاَ يَجِدُونَ إِلاَّ جُهْدَهُمْ﴾,
meaning Abū ʿUqayl. Al-juhd is the dialect of the people of the Ḥijāz, as is al-wujd; the dialect of others is al-jahd and al-wajd.

farraa:83-83.t: His saying: ﴿فَٱقْعُدُواْ مَعَ ٱلْخَالِفِينَ﴾: of men [one says] khulūf and khālifūn; and of women khawālif: those who stay behind in the house and do not leave. It is also said ʿabd khālif and ṣāḥib khālif ("a contrary slave", "a contrary companion") when he is contrary (mukhālif).

farraa:90-90.t: His saying: ﴿وَجَآءَ ٱلْمُعَذِّرُونَ﴾: they are those who have an excuse. In meaning it is al-muʿtadhirūn (those who excuse themselves), but the tāʾ was assimilated to the dhāl and both became a doubled dhāl, as in yadhdhakkarūna and yadhdhakkaru. It is like (يخَصِّمونَ) for whoever gives the khāʾ a fatḥa; likewise the ʿayn was given a fatḥa because the vowel of the tāʾ passed to the ʿayn; it was — and Allah knows best — al-muʿtadhirūn. As for al-muʿadhdhir on the pattern of mufaʿʿil, he is one who makes excuses without [having] an excuse. Muḥammad related to us: al-Farrāʾ related to us, saying: Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh related to me from al-Kalbī from Abū Ṣāliḥ from Ibn ʿAbbās; and Abū Ḥafṣ al-Kharrāz from Juwaybir from al-Ḍaḥḥāk from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he read (المُعْذِرون), and said: "May Allah curse the muʿadhdhirīn", meaning those who make excuses without an excuse; and al-muʿdhir is one who has gone to the utmost limit of excuse. Al-muʿtadhir may have the meaning of al-muʿdhir, and may be one who has no excuse. Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, said concerning those who have no excuse: ﴿يَعْتَذِرُونَ إِلَيْكُمْ إِذَا رَجَعْتُمْ إِلَيْهِمْ﴾.

farraa:92-92.t:
His saying: ﴿حَزَناً أَلاَّ يَجِدُواْ﴾: (يَجِدُوا) is in the position of the accusative by أن. It would [also be permissible] if it were nominative, making (لا) in the manner of (ليس), as if you said: "in grief that they do not find (أن ليس يجدون) what to spend". Like it is His saying: ﴿أَفَلاَ يَرَوْنَ أَنْ لاَ يَرْجِعُ إلَيْهمْ قَوْلاً﴾, and His saying: ﴿وحَسِبُوا أَنْ لاَ تَكُونَ فِتْنَةٌ﴾.
Wherever (ليس) is suitable in place of (لا), you may put the verb after (لا) in the nominative or in the accusative.
[Translator's note: the apodosis of «ولو كانت رفعا» ("and if it were nominative…") is not stated in the source; "it would also be permissible" is supplied from the context.]

farraa:94-94.t:
His saying: ﴿يَعْتَذِرُونَ إِلَيْكُمْ إِذَا رَجَعْتُمْ إِلَيْهِمْ﴾, then He said: (لاَ تَعْتَذِرُوا): you have no excuse. Labīd said, in the sense of iʿtidhār as iʿdhār, when he made them one:
وقُوما فقولا بالذى قد علمتما * ولا تخمِشا وجها ولا تحلقا الشعر
إلى الحول ثم اسمُ السلام عليكما * ومَنْ يبكِ حولا كاملا فقد اعتذر
(Rise, you two, and say what you know; do not scratch a face nor shave the hair — until a year [has passed]; then the name of peace be upon you both: whoever weeps a full year has done all that excuse requires.)
He means: فقد أعذر.

farraa:97-97.t:
His saying: ﴿ٱلأَعْرَابُ أَشَدُّ كُفْراً وَنِفَاقاً﴾ was revealed about a group of the Bedouins of Asad and Ghaṭafān and those living near Medina. (أجدر) is like your saying aḥrā and akhlaq ("more fitting", "more likely").
﴿وَأَجْدَرُ أَلاَّ يَعْلَمُواْ﴾: the position of (أن) is accusative. Wherever (أن) comes and the speech before it is complete with what it has put in the genitive, nominative or accusative, (أن) is in the position of the accusative; as in your saying: أتيتك أنّك محسن ("I came to you because you are good"), قمت أنك مسىء ("I stood because you are bad"), and ثَبَتُّ عنك أنك صديق وصاحب. It has become clear to you that (أن) is in the position of the accusative because you can put the maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of (أن) and it is accusative; do you not see that you say: أتيتك إحسانَك ("I came to you for your goodness")? So الإحسان, by its accusative, shows the accusative of أن; and likewise the other two.
As for His saying: ﴿وَأَجْدَرُ أَلاَّ يَعْلَمُواْ﴾, putting the maṣdar in the place of (أن) is ugly, because akhlaq and ajdar require the future of verbs, and so with (أن) the future is made clear; whereas if you put a maṣdar in place of (أن), its futurity is not made clear, and that is ugly. And (أن) is in the position of the accusative in every case; do you not see that you say أظن أنك قائم ("I think that you are standing") and judge (أن) to be accusative, while it is not proper to say أظن قيامك ("I think your standing")? So aẓunnu is parallel to khalīq, to ʿasā, (jadīr), ajdar and their inflected forms as regards (أن).

farraa:98-98.t:
His saying: ﴿وَيَتَرَبَّصُ بِكُمُ ٱلدَّوَائِرَ﴾ means: death and being killed.
Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, says: ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ دَآئِرَةُ ٱلسَّوْءِ﴾. Giving the sīn of (السوء) a fatḥa is the proper form of speech and the reading of most of the readers. Mujāhid gave the sīn a ḍamma in two places: here and in Sūrat al-Fatḥ. Whoever says "دائرة السَّوء" intends the maṣdar of suʾtuhu: sawʾan, masāʾatan, masāʾiyatan and sawāʾiyatan; these are maṣdars. Whoever gives the sīn a ḍamma makes it a noun, as you say: "upon him is the turn of trial and punishment." It is not permissible to put a ḍamma on the ʿayn in His saying: ﴿ما كان أبوكِ امرَأَ سَوْء﴾, nor in His saying: ﴿وظننتُمْ ظَنَّ السَّوْء﴾, because it is the opposite of your saying: "this is a man of truth (ṣidq)" and "a garment of truth [i.e. of good quality]". So al-sawʾ here has no sense of punishment or trial, such that it would take a ḍamma.
[Translator's note: by "the ʿayn" the author evidently means the first vowelled letter of the word, i.e. the sīn of السَّوْء; translated as written.]

farraa:100-100.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلسَّابِقُونَ ٱلأَوَّلُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُهَاجِرِينَ وَٱلأَنْصَارِ﴾: if you wish you put الأنصار in the genitive, meaning: of the Emigrants and of the Anṣār. If you wish you put (الأنصار) in the nominative, made to follow His saying (والسابقون). Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī read it so. (والذين أتبعوهم بإحسان): those who did good after them until the Day of Resurrection. (السابقون والذين اتبعوهم) are nominative by the pronoun referring back to them in His saying رضى الله عنهم.
[Translator's note: the sentence «وقد قرأها الحسن البصرىّ» ("al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī read it") is followed in the source directly by the next quotation; it presumably refers to the nominative reading والأنصارُ. The source also has «أتبعوهم» in the first quotation and «اتبعوهم» in the second; reproduced as written.]

farraa:101-101.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمِنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْمَدِينَةِ مَرَدُواْ عَلَى ٱلنِّفَاقِ﴾: they became inured to it and persisted in it (marūwū ʿalayhi), as in your saying: tamarradū (they became obstinate).
His saying: ﴿سَنُعَذِّبُهُم مَّرَّتَيْنِ﴾: he said: by being killed and by the punishment of the grave.

farraa:102-102.t:
His saying: ﴿خَلَطُواْ عَمَلاً صَالِحاً﴾: He says: they went out to Badr and were present at it. It is also said: the righteous deed is their repentance from staying behind from the campaign of Tabūk.
﴿وَآخَرَ سَيِّئاً﴾: their staying behind on the day of Tabūk. ﴿عَسَى ٱللَّهُ﴾: ʿasā (perhaps) from Allah is binding, if Allah wills. These men had tied themselves to the pillars of the mosque and sworn not to leave that until their repentance was revealed. When it was revealed they said: "O Messenger of Allah, take our wealth in thanks for our repentance." He said: "I will not do so until Qurʾān is revealed to me about that." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed His saying: ﴿خُذْ مِنْ أَمْوَالِهِمْ صَدَقَةً﴾.

farraa:103-103.t:
His saying: ﴿خُذْ مِنْ أَمْوَالِهِمْ صَدَقَةً﴾: so he took part of it.
Then He said: ﴿تُطَهِّرُهُمْ وَتُزَكِّيهِمْ بِهَا وَصَلِّ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾: ask forgiveness for them, for your asking forgiveness for them is something their hearts find rest in, and they are reassured that Allah has accepted their repentance. It has also been read (صلواتك) [in the plural].
The singular al-ṣalāt is more common.
[Translator's note: the source has «استغفر فهم», evidently for «استغفر لهم» ("ask forgiveness for them").]

farraa:106-106.t:
His saying: ﴿وَآخَرُونَ مُرْجَوْنَ لأَمْرِ ٱللَّهِ﴾: they are three named persons who stayed behind from the Prophet ﷺ on the campaign of Tabūk. When he returned he said: "What is your excuse?" They said: "We have no excuse but sin." So they were held in suspense until their repentance was revealed in….
[Translator's note: the sentence breaks off in the source after «فى» ("in").]

farraa:107-107.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّخَذُواْ مَسْجِداً ضِرَاراً﴾: they are Banū ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf of the Anṣār, who built their mosque to rival and harm the mosque of Qubāʾ.
The mosque of Qubāʾ was the first mosque built on piety. When the Prophet ﷺ came back from the campaign of Tabūk, he ordered the mosque of dissension to be burnt and demolished.
[Translator's note: the mosque of ḍirār is usually attributed to a group of hypocrites who built it near Banū ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf, whose own mosque was that of Qubāʾ; the source's wording is translated as it stands.]

farraa:108-108.t:
His saying: ﴿لاَ تَقُمْ فِيهِ أَبَداً﴾ means the mosque of Banū ʿAmr. Then the speech breaks off and He said: ﴿لَّمَسْجِدٌ أُسِّسَ عَلَى ٱلتَّقْوَىٰ مِنْ أَوَّلِ يَوْمٍ أَحَقُّ أَن تَقُومَ فِيهِ﴾. Then He said: (فيه رجال). The first [فيه] is attached as a complement to His saying (تقوم), and the second has put الرجال in the nominative.
His saying: ﴿أُسِّسَ﴾ and (أُسِّسَ) [is also read]; and asās and āsās are permissible. It seems to me that I have heard it in recitation.

farraa:110-110.t: His saying: ﴿لاَ يَزَالُ بُنْيَانُهُمُ﴾ means the mosque of hypocrisy; (رِيبَةً): it is said: doubt. (إلا أن تَقَطَّع) and (تُقَطَّع): its meaning is: unless they die. Al-Ḥasan read (إلى أن تَقَطَّع), in the sense of ḥattā (until), that is: until they are cut to pieces. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is (ولو قُطِّعت قلوبُهم), a proof for whoever reads (إلا أن تقطع) with a ḍamma on the tāʾ.

farraa:111-111.t:
His saying: ﴿فَيَقْتُلُونَ وَيُقْتَلُونَ﴾: [in] the reading of the companions of ʿAbd Allāh, they put the passive [lit. the mafʿūl bihi] before the active [lit. the fāʿil]. The reading of the generality is (فَيَقْتُلون ويُقْتَلون).
His saying: ﴿وَعْداً عَلَيْهِ حَقّاً﴾ comes out of His saying: ﴿بِأَنَّ لَهُمُ ٱلّجَنَّةَ﴾. It is like your saying: علىَّ ألف درهم عِدّةً صحيحةً ("I owe a thousand dirhams, as a true promise"). The nominative would be permissible if it were said.
[Translator's note: the source has «خاج», evidently a misprint for «خارج» ("comes out of"). The Qurʾānic quotation ﴿فَيَقْتُلُونَ وَيُقْتَلُونَ﴾ and the "reading of the generality" are printed identically in the source, without vowel distinction of the order; the Ibn Masʿūd/Kufan reading is known as فيُقتَلون ويَقتُلون.]

farraa:112-112.t:
His saying: ﴿ٱلتَّائِبُونَ ٱلْعَابِدُونَ﴾ was begun anew in the nominative because the verse before it is complete and the speech breaks off, so a new beginning (istiʾnāf) is good.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is "التائبين العابدين", in the position of the genitive, because it is an adjective (naʿt) of the believers: He bought from the believers who repent. It is also permissible for (التائبين) to be in the position of the accusative by way of praise (madḥ), as [the poetess] said:
لا يَبْعَدَنْ قومى الذين هُم * سُمّ العُدَاة وآفَةُ الجُزْرِ
النازلين بكل معتَرك * والطيّبينَ معاقِدَ الأزْر
(May my people not perish, who are poison to enemies and a bane to slaughter-camels; who alight in every battle-field, and pure where their waist-wrappers are tied.)

farraa:115-115.t: His saying: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ ٱللَّهُ لِيُضِلَّ قَوْماً بَعْدَ إِذْ هَدَاهُمْ﴾: the Muslims asked the Prophet ﷺ about those Muslims who had died while praying towards the first qibla and holding wine lawful before it was forbidden. They said: "O Messenger of Allah, did our brothers die astray?" So Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, revealed: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ ٱللَّهُ لِيُضِلَّ قَوْماً بَعْدَ إِذْ هَدَاهُمْ حَتَّىٰ يُبَيِّنَ لَهُم مَّا يَتَّقُونَ﴾. He says: they were not astray, for they had not been turned away from the first qibla, and the prohibition of wine had not been revealed to them.

farraa:117-117.t: His saying: ﴿لَقَدْ تَابَ الله عَلَىٰ ٱلنَّبِيِّ وَٱلْمُهَاجِرِينَ وَٱلأَنصَارِ﴾, and His saying: ﴿مِن بَعْدِ مَا كَادَ يَزِيغُ﴾ and (كاد تزيغ). [Whoever] says (كاد يزيغ) puts in (كاد يزيِغ) a noun [i.e. an implied subject] like the one in His saying: ﴿عسى أن يكونوا خيرا منهم﴾, and makes (يزيغ), by which القلوب is put in the nominative, masculine; as Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, said: ﴿لن ينالَ اللهَ لحومُهَا﴾ and ﴿لا يحل لك النساء من بعد﴾. Whoever says (تزيغ) makes the verb of the hearts feminine, as He said: ﴿نريد أن نأكل مِنها وتطمئن قلوبنا﴾, and that is the proper form of speech; He did not say (يطمئن). Every verb belonging to a plural, masculine or feminine, you may, if you wish, make feminine when you put it first, and if you wish make masculine.

farraa:118-118.t:
His saying: ﴿وَعَلَى ٱلثَّلاَثَةِ ٱلَّذِينَ خُلِّفُواْ﴾: they are Kaʿb ibn Mālik, Bilāl ibn Umayya and Murāra.
[Translator's note: the source has «بلال بن أمية»; the Companion is usually named Hilāl ibn Umayya.]

farraa:120-120.t: His saying: ﴿وَلاَ يَطَأُونَ مَوْطِئاً﴾: by al-mawṭiʾ He means the land. ﴿ولا يقطعون واديا﴾ in their going and coming, but it is written for them.

farraa:122-122.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ لِيَنفِرُواْ كَآفَّةً﴾: when the Muslims were reproached for staying behind from the campaign of Tabūk, [and] the Prophet ﷺ began to send out raiding parties, they would all go out together, so that the Prophet ﷺ would be left alone. So Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, revealed: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ لِيَنفِرُواْ كَآفَّةً﴾, meaning: all together, leaving you alone.
Then He said: ﴿فَلَوْلاَ نَفَرَ﴾, its meaning being: why did there not go out ﴿مِن كُلِّ فِرْقَةٍ مِّنْهُمْ طَآئِفَةٌ﴾, so that those remaining who stayed behind might gain understanding and preserve [and teach] their people what was revealed of the Qurʾān to the Prophet ﷺ.
﴿وَلِيُنذِرُواْ قَوْمَهُمْ﴾: He says: to give them understanding. It has also been said about it that the Bedouins of Asad came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in Medina, so prices rose and they filled the roads with filth. So Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, revealed: ﴿فَلَوْلاَ نَفَرَ﴾: He says: why did not a party of them go out, then return to their people and tell them what they had learned?

farraa:123-123.t: His saying: ﴿يَلُونَكُمْ مِّنَ ٱلْكُفَّارِ﴾ means: the nearest, then the next nearest.

farraa:124-124.t: His saying: ﴿وَإِذَا مَآ أُنزِلَتْ سُورَةٌ فَمِنْهُمْ مَّن يَقُولُ﴾ means the hypocrites; some of them say to others: "Has this increased you in faith?" So Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, revealed: ﴿فأما الذين آمنوا فزادتهم إيمانا...وأما الذين فى قلوبهم مرض فزادتهم رِجْساً إلى رِجسهم﴾. The sickness here is hypocrisy.

farraa:126-126.t:
His saying: ﴿أَوَلاَ يَرَوْنَ﴾, and (ويّروا) with tāʾ. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "أو لا ترى أَنهم". The Arabs say أَلا ترى ("do you not see?") to a group and to one person alike, as an expression of wonder; just as it is said "ذلك أزكى لهم" and "ذلكم"; likewise (أَلا ترى) and (الا ترون).
[Translator's note: «ويّروا» appears to be a corrupted spelling of the tāʾ reading «أَوَلا تَرَوْن»; reproduced as written.]

farraa:127-127.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِذَا مَآ أُنزِلَتْ سُورَةٌ﴾ in which they were mentioned and their faults [exposed], some of them said to others: ﴿هَلْ يَرَاكُمْ مِّنْ أَحَدٍ﴾ if you stand up [and leave]? Then if it was possible for them to stand up, they stood up.
That is His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ ٱنصَرَفُواْ صَرَفَ ٱللَّهُ قُلُوبَهُم﴾, an imprecation against them.
[Translator's note: «فإن لهم القيام» is probably for «فإن أمكنهم القيام» ("if standing up was possible for them"); translated in that sense.]

farraa:128-128.t:
His saying: ﴿لَقَدْ جَآءَكُمْ رَسُولٌ مِّنْ أَنفُسِكُمْ﴾: He says: there remained no clan of the Arabs but had a share in his birth. That is His saying ﴿مِّنْ أَنفُسِكُمْ﴾.
His saying: ﴿عَزِيزٌ عَلَيْهِ مَا عَنِتُّمْ﴾: (ما) is in the position of the nominative; its meaning is: your suffering is grievous to him. Had it been accusative — "عزيزا عليه ما عنتم حريصا رءوفا رحيما" — it would be correct, on the basis of His saying: "there has come to you [a messenger] thus". And al-ḥirṣ (eager concern) is being grudging that they should enter the Fire.
